GCLKGeneric Clock Controllerp. 134

CTRLAControl Ap. 136

offset 0x00 · 8 bits · reset 0x00 · access R/W · pac write-protection, write-synchronized

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
0SWRSTR/W0Write 1 to return every GCLK register to its power-reset state, except generic clocks and their generators locked by PCHCTRLm.WRTLOCK = 1; writing 0 does nothing. The reset is synchronized, so it takes time; CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST both clear when it is done.
0No reset in progress.
1Reset in progress.

SYNCBUSYSynchronization Busyp. 137

offset 0x04 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
10:2GENCTRLnone per bitR0x0One bit per GENCTRLn: goes to 1 when synchronization of GENCTRLn across clock domains begins, and back to 0 when it ends or when a clock switch completes.
0SWRSTR0Goes to 1 when synchronization of CTRLA.SWRST across clock domains begins, and back to 0 when it ends.

GENCTRLnGenerator Controlp. 138

offset 0x20 · 9 copies, every 0x04 · 32 bits · reset 0b00000000000000000000000x000xxxxx · access R/W · pac write-protection, write-synchronized

  • One register per generic clock generator n, n = 0..8.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:16DIVR/W0x0Division value for the generator, read according to DIVSEL. Generators 0 and 2 to 8 use 8 bits (DIV[7:0]), generator 1 uses 16 bits (DIV[15:0]); bits written beyond that are ignored.
13RUNSTDBYR/W0Keeps the generator running in standby while it drives its GCLK_IO pin. Does nothing when GENCTRLn.OE is 0; the generator then runs only when a peripheral asks for its clock.
0Generator stops in standby; the GCLK_IO level follows GENCTRL.OOV.
1Generator keeps running in standby and keeps driving GCLK_IO.
12DIVSELR/W0Chooses how DIV turns into the division of the generator's source clock. For no division, DIVSEL must be 0 with GENCTRLn.DIV at 0 or 1.
0Output = source frequency / GENCTRLn.DIV.
1Output = source frequency / 2^(GENCTRLn.DIV+1).
11OER/W0Drives the generator clock out on its GCLK_IO pin, provided GCLK_IO is not chosen as the generator's source in GENCTRLn.SRC.
0GCLK_IO carries no generator clock.
1GCLK_IO carries the generator clock, unless GCLK_IO is the source chosen in GENCTRLn.SRC.
10OOVR/W0Level driven on GCLK_IO while the generator is off or OE is 0, provided GCLK_IO is not chosen as the generator's source in GENCTRLn.SRC.
0GCLK_IO low while the generator is off or OE is 0.
1GCLK_IO high while the generator is off or OE is 0.
9IDCR/W0Evens the generator output's duty cycle to 50/50 when the division factor is odd.
0Duty cycle not evened for odd division factors.
1Duty cycle 50/50.
8GENENR/WxTurns the generator on or off.
0Generator off.
1Generator on.
4:0SRCR/WxClock source of the generator. A power reset sets GENCTRL0 to 0x00000106 and the others to 0x00000000. A user reset does the same, except a generator feeding a locked peripheral channel (PCHCTRLm.WRTLOCK = 1) keeps its GENCTRL.
0x00XOSCXOSC oscillator.
0x01GCLK_INGCLK_IO input pin.
0x02GCLK_GEN1Output of generic clock generator 1.
0x03OSCULP32KOSCULP32K oscillator.
0x04OSC32KOSC32K oscillator.
0x05XOSC32KXOSC32K oscillator.
0x06OSC16MOSC16M oscillator.

offset 0x02 · per channel, every 0x10 · 16 bits · access -

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:0BTCNT-0x016-bit block transfer count, counted down by one per beat. The running count is written to the channel's write-back entry when the channel loses priority, is suspended, or is disabled (by completion, a transfer error, or software).

offset 0x04 · per channel, every 0x10 · 32 bits · access -

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:0SRCADDR-0x0Source address for the block. With BTCTRL.SRCINC=0 it is the address of the last beat. offset 0x08 · per channel, every 0x10 · 32 bits · access -

NVMCTRLNon-Volatile Memory Controllerp. 462

CTRLAControl Ap. 463

offset 0x00 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W · pac write-protection

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:8CMDEXR/W0x0Key field: writing 0xA5 here, in the same write as CMD, runs the command in CMD. With any other value the whole write is dropped and STATUS.PROGE is set; PROGE is also set when the previous command has not finished. INTFLAG.READY must be 1 when a command is given. An APB command arriving in the same cycle as an AHB access waits for the AHB access, and runs once both the AHB bus and the NVM block go idle. Bit 0 reads 1 until the command is given. ADDR.ADDR counts in 16-bit half-words.
6:0CMDR/W0x0Selects the NVM command run when the CMDEX key is written.
0x00-0x01-Reserved.
0x02ERErases the NVM main-array row that ADDR points to.
0x03-Reserved.
0x04WPWrites the page buffer into the page that ADDR points to.
0x05EARErases the auxiliary row that ADDR points to; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the security bit is clear.
0x06WAPWrites the page buffer into the auxiliary page that ADDR points to; allowed only on the User Configuration Row and only while the security bit is clear.
0x07-0x19-Reserved.
0x1ARWWEEERErases the RWWEE-array row that ADDR points to.
0x1B-Reserved.
0x1CRWWEEWPWrites the page buffer into the RWWEE-array page that ADDR points to.
0x1D-0x3F-Reserved.
0x40LRLocks the lock region holding the address in ADDR.
0x41URUnlocks the lock region holding the address in ADDR.
0x42SPRMPuts the NVM into power reduction mode.
0x43CPRMTakes the NVM out of power reduction mode.
0x44PBCEmpties the page buffer.
0x45SSBSets the security bit, by writing 0x00 into the first byte of the lockbit row.
0x46INVALLInvalidates every cache line.

10:0ADDRR/W0x0Writing an address starts an action that depends on STATUS.BUSSTATE. UNKNOWN: MB in INTFLAG and BUSERR in STATUS get set and nothing more happens. BUSY: the Host waits for IDLE. IDLE: the Host sends a start condition and the address; on ACK it holds SCL low and sets STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB. OWNER: a repeated start follows, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; this write is made while one of the INTFLAG bits MB or SB is 1. A write clears BUSERR and ARBLOST in STATUS and MB and SB in INTFLAG. Reads never disturb the bus. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

The value reads back at once and SYNCBUSY.COMPCTRLn goes to 1; the change takes effect after synchronization, when SYNCBUSY.COMPCTRLn returns to 0. While ENABLE is 1 the other COMPCTRLn bits are locked, until ENABLE is written 0 and that write has synchronized.

INTFLAGInterrupt Flag Status and Clearp. 1057

offset 0x06 · 8 bits · reset 0x00 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
3EMPTY1R/W0Goes to 1 when the DAC1 data buffer has emptied, raising an interrupt if INTENSET.EMPTY1 is 1. Cleared by writing 1 here or by writing DATA1 or DATABUF1; writing 0 does nothing.
2EMPTY0R/W0Goes to 1 when the DAC0 data buffer has emptied, raising an interrupt if INTENSET.EMPTY0 is 1. Cleared by writing 1 here or by writing DATA0 or DATABUF0; writing 0 does nothing.
1UNDERRUN1R/W0Goes to 1 when a START1 event arrives before new data has reached the DAC1 data buffer, raising an interrupt if INTENSET.UNDERRUN1 is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.
0UNDERRUN0R/W0Goes to 1 when a START0 event arrives before new data has reached the DAC0 data buffer, raising an interrupt if INTENSET.UNDERRUN0 is 1. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.
